title: Claude fallback implementer: shell rules in the brief, a short denied count in status
lead: When the Claude implementer (matrix row r3) stands in for Codex, ork gives it two fixes. (a) Its brief says which shell commands it may use and how (Claude only). (c) `ork status` shows a short count of denied commands instead of their text. Part (b), one automatic nudge on a report shape pause, was dropped on 2026-11-04 because S275 landed that retry; the letters (a) and (c) are kept so earlier notes and decisions still match.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Wave 5 (2026-11-02, owner's report of S238 and S190, which ork ran): Codex was out of credits at launch, ork fell back to the Claude implementer (matrix row r3, claude sonnet high), and both runs paused with `report shape: no "Tests: N passed, M failed" line; no "## Owner needed" section; next: ork retry RUN`. The status line then printed the denied Bash commands. The owner decided on 2026-11-02 (interactive) that this goes in pass v1.1 and chose three parts, called option (3): (a) shell rules for the Claude implementer, (b) one automatic nudge on a report shape pause, (c) a short denied count in status. Whether ork should hold an engine-slice run until Codex's out-until time instead of falling back to Claude is not decided and is not part of this slice.

Owner 2026-11-04 (ork S287 Q2, "drop-part-b", accepted): part (b) is out of this slice. S275 (landed on main as 9865f1e) already retries a shape-only report error once, in the same round and session, for the implementer (and its finish step), reviewer, gate, architect and UI pass (`runRound`, `AutomaticShapeRetry` at `internal/engine/round.go:558` and `:739`; `docs/design.md:597-602`). A second retry path beside it would duplicate that. This slice is now parts (a) and (c).

What the code at HEAD of main shows (verified 2026-11-02; re-verified 2026-11-04 at b9b905c and 2026-11-07 at a1114e2, line numbers updated):

- The Claude implementer runs on an allowlist. `DefaultImplementerAllowlist` (`internal/engine/perm.go:24-36`) holds `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Edit`, `Write` and prefix patterns such as `Bash(slicer *)`, `Bash(go -C * test*)`, `Bash(gofmt *)`, plus `Bash(<check command>*)`. It has no `sed`, `python3`, `cd`, `grep` or `rg` entry. A registry `permissions.implementer` list replaces the default as is (`ResolvePermission`, `perm.go:47-71`; `TestImplementerGetsTheRegistryAllowlistAsIs`, `perm_test.go:36`). The Claude adapter passes the list as `--allowedTools a,b --permission-prompts none` (`internal/agent/claude/args.go:59`), and Codex gets `workspace-write` or `read-only` instead (`internal/agent/codex/codex.go:53-56`). So a `sed -i`, a `python3` heredoc or a `cd X && ...` command matches no default pattern, and it is denied for Claude and runs for Codex.
- Since S277 (done, commit 6195cc5) the brief does list the allowlist, for every vendor. `BriefInput.Allow` (`internal/engine/brief.go:22`) is set from `perm.Allow` in `runRound` (`internal/engine/round.go:298-302`; `perm` is resolved at `round.go:254`; the runner request gets `Allowlist: perm.Allow` at `round.go:382`). For a write role, `doneWhen` (`brief.go:153`) adds to `## Done when` the item "Allowed forms, verbatim: ...; any other command is denied; no pipes, no cd, no env prefix unless an entry allows it." (`brief.go:166-167`). It does not say to change files with the Edit and Write tools, and it does not name `sed -i`, scripts, heredocs, redirects, `&&` or `;`. Commit 7bb435b (S280) added Grok-only lines to the read-only branch of `doneWhen` (`brief.go:160-165`); write roles are untouched, so it does not overlap with part (a). `ork run` prints the allowlist (`internal/cli/run.go:200`). So most of part (a) is already in place; see Open question Q1.
- The role prompt is one file for every vendor. `roles.Prompt(name)` takes no vendor (`internal/roles/roles.go:45-54`), and `internal/roles/prompts/implementer.md` is embedded and canonical (`roles.prompts`, adj 29). `TestNoClaudeCodeOnlyMechanics` (`internal/roles/roles_test.go:248`) forbids the word Bash in a prompt. The brief builder already branches on the vendor (`brief.go:100`, the UI pass skills line). So a Claude-only line belongs in `BuildBrief`, and `implementer.md` stays as it is (Codex unchanged).
- The status line prints at most three denials in full and then `and N more` (`source.DenialsText`, `internal/source/source.go:282-287`; used at `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:102`). Each denial text is `Tool: command` capped at 200 characters (`internal/agent/claude/types.go:74,82-101`; `internal/runrec/record.go:81-92`), so three Bash denials can fill several lines. The daemon builds `EngineRun.Denials` as distinct texts in first-seen order with ` xN` for repeats (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1329-1345`, field at `internal/source/source.go:274`). The TUI uses the same `DenialsText` (`internal/tui/overview.go:389,995`).

Historical, part (b) only (2026-11-02, before S275; no longer true at HEAD): a shape error paused the run at once, and `ork retry RUN` resumed the role with a `## Report shape` section. S275 replaced that with the automatic retry above.

Not verified (the run logs are outside the workspace and were not read):

- Why the two final reports lacked the shape. A report file that is missing or empty falls back to the vendor's final message text (`Engine.readReport`, `internal/engine/round.go:650`), which would lack both parts; that is consistent with what happened but not shown.
- Which exact commands Sonnet was denied. The five kinds the owner named (a `python3` heredoc edit, `sed -i` on a Go file, `grep` into `sed`, `cd` then `sed`, `rg` pipelines) match no default pattern, as above. Whether the ork project's registry entry holds `Bash(rg *)` is not shown in the workspace; the default list has no `rg`.
- That Claude Code's matcher refuses a pipe, `cd`, a heredoc or `sed -i` after an allowed prefix. That is Claude Code's behaviour, not ork's; the repo's fixtures show only a denied `Write` (`testdata/vendors/claude/04-allowlist-denies-write.stdout`).
- The status line printing "every" command. At HEAD it prints at most three, each up to 200 characters, then a count.

Design choices (*proposed* until an adj record decides them):

- The shell rules are a section of the Claude implementer's brief, built from the allowlist the role really has, not text in the shared prompt.
- `ork status` counts distinct denial texts and shows the first one cut to 40 characters. `--json` and the TUI are unchanged.
- (Dropped 2026-11-04 with part (b): the nudge's scope, its not-a-round rule and its budget rule. S275 settled those for its own retry.)

Open question Q1 (open, 2026-11-07; owner to answer): S277's `## Done when` already gives every write role its allowlist verbatim and forbids pipes and `cd`. What is left of part (a)?
- (a1) Drop part (a); the slice becomes part (c) only.
- (a2) Keep a Claude-only addition, but as extra `doneWhen` items beside the S277 "Allowed forms" line (change files with Edit and Write; no `sed -i`, scripts, heredocs, redirects, `&&` or `;`), using the existing `Allow` field; no new section and no new field.
- (a3) Keep the `## Shell commands` section as specced below, built from `in.Allow`, and leave S277's line as it is (the allowlist then appears twice).
Recommendation: (a2). It adds only the rules S277 lacks, keeps one place for them, and avoids repeating the list. The Failing tests and Implement sections below are written for (a3) with the field renamed to the existing `Allow`; under (a2) the tests check `## Done when` items instead of a section.

Owner decisions (interactive question, 2026-11-02): the three parts were the whole slice (part (b) since dropped, above); the answers stated in this spec are accepted as written (the denied count reads as stated; the nudge answers no longer apply); the spec check keeps its own existing retry; ork keeps falling back to the Claude implementer when Codex is out (it does not hold the run). Related owner rule, 2026-11-02: for Grok and any other vendor, do not pin a model version unless the owner asks; default to the vendor's latest.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Part (a), `internal/engine/brief_test.go`:

- TestClaudeImplementerBriefHasShellRules: `BriefInput{Role: RoleImplementer, Vendor: "claude", Allow: DefaultImplementerAllowlist("go test ./...")}`. The brief has a `## Shell commands` section that says to change files with the Edit and Write tools, to run one plain command per shell call, and not to use pipes, `cd`, heredocs, scripts or `sed -i`. It lists every `Bash(...)` entry of the allowlist as the pattern inside the parentheses (`slicer *`, `go -C * test*`, `go test ./...*`) and the other entries as tool names. Fails first: there is no section (S277's `## Done when` line lists the forms but not these rules).
- TestShellRulesOnlyForTheClaudeImplementer: no `## Shell commands` section and none of the new rule lines, for a codex implementer, an empty vendor, `Claude` (case-sensitive), and a claude reviewer, gate, architect, UI pass and spec-check. Passes today; it guards the vendor and role conditions (mutation step 8).
- TestShellSectionFollowsTheRegistryAllowlist: a list of `Edit` and `Bash(dotnet test*)` shows `dotnet test*` and `Edit` and none of the default entries (`slicer *` is absent). A list with no `Bash(` entry says the role has no shell commands. A check command with a backtick or newline in its entry stays inside a fence that is longer than any backtick run in it (the rule of `fenceFor`, `brief.go:42`). Fails first: no section.
- TestFinishStepBriefKeepsTheShellSection: with `Finish: true` the section is still present (the finish step runs `slicer` commands). Fails first: no section.

Part (a), `internal/engine/fallback_test.go` or `internal/engine/brief_test.go` (use `fallbackHarness` at `fallback_test.go:81`):

- TestClaudeFallbackBriefListsTheRealAllowlist: codex row exits `ExitOutOfCredits`, the claude row runs. The claude request's brief has `## Shell commands` and every `Bash(...)` pattern of that request's `Allowlist` (the runner request field, `round.go:382`); the codex request's brief has no such section. Fails first: the section is missing.

Part (c), `internal/cli`:

- TestStatusCountsDeniedCommands: five denials, the first a 120-character `Bash: ...` text. `ork status` prints `(denied: 5 commands, first: ` plus the first text cut to 40 characters ending in `...`, then `)`; none of the other four texts appears; the line has no text beyond the cut. Fails first: it prints `A, B, C and 2 more` style text.
- TestStatusDeniedOneCommandIsSingular: one denial of 12 characters prints `(denied: 1 command, first: Write: /x.txt)` with no cut. Fails first: old format.
- TestStatusDeniedCutsOnRunesNotBytes: a first denial with multi-byte characters is cut on a rune boundary (valid UTF-8). Fails first: old format.
- TestStatusJSONKeepsEveryDenial: `ork status --json` prints the daemon's `denials` array exactly as received (five long texts). Fails first: passes today; keep it as a guard for "the data in --json is unchanged".
- The pinned texts in `TestStatusBoundsDenials` (`cli_test.go:1247`), `TestStatusPrintsEngineStateAndWait` (`run_test.go:300`) and `TestStatusSectionsAndNeedsRows` (`run_test.go:385`) change to the new format. `internal/tui` tests and `testdata/golden/engine-denials-100x30.txt` stay byte for byte as they are.

(Part (b)'s `nudge_test.go` tests were removed on 2026-11-04 with part (b); S275's tests in `internal/engine/round_test.go` cover the automatic shape retry.)

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Tests first. Watch each fail for the stated reason before the product code. Wait for the owner's answer to Q1 (Why) before part (a); part (c) does not depend on it.

Do not touch: `internal/roles/prompts/implementer.md` and every other prompt, `internal/source/source.go` (`DenialsText` stays for the TUI), `internal/tui` and `testdata/golden`, `internal/daemon/runs.go` (the `denials` data and `--json` stay as they are), `internal/engine/speccheck.go`, `internal/engine/perm.go`, and S275's shape retry in `round.go` (`AutomaticShapeRetry`).

1. Part (a), tests: write the four brief tests and the fallback test. Add the section (or, under Q1 option (a2), the `doneWhen` items) last.
2. Part (a), product: use the existing `BriefInput.Allow` (S277); add no field. In `BuildBrief`, after the "Checks ork runs" block and before `doneWhen` (`brief.go:139`), when `in.Role == RoleImplementer && in.Vendor == "claude"` (case-sensitive, as `brief.go:100`), write `## Shell commands`. Under Q1 option (a2), add the rule sentences below as `doneWhen` items after the "Allowed forms" item (`brief.go:167`) instead, without the list. Text (*proposed*): "ork limits your shell to the commands below. Any other command is denied and does not run. Change files with the Edit and Write tools only: no `sed -i`, no scripts (python or others), no heredocs, no redirects into files. Run one plain command per shell call: no pipes, no `&&` or `;`, no command substitution, no `cd` (use absolute paths, `go -C DIR` and `git -C DIR`). If a command is denied, use an allowed form; do not retry it another way." Then "Tools: " plus the non-Bash entries, and the `Bash(...)` entries as their inner patterns, one per line, in one fenced block (fence length by `fenceFor`, `brief.go:42`; a trailing `*` means any further text). An allowlist with no Bash entry says the role has no shell commands. Do not rewrite the entries. `runRound` already sets `Allow: perm.Allow` (`round.go:302`). A read-only role has no list, and the section is not written for it.
3. Part (a), docs: in `docs/design.md`, in the S277 `## Done when` paragraph (`:802-812`), say what the `claude` implementer's brief adds about shell commands, and that the prompt stays vendor-neutral; mark it *proposed*.
4. Part (c), tests: write the three status tests and the JSON guard; update the three pinned old texts.
5. Part (c), product, in `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:102`: replace `source.DenialsText(r.Denials)` with a small helper in `internal/cli` that prints `(denied: N command[s], first: TEXT)`, where N is `len(r.Denials)` (distinct texts), `TEXT` is `r.Denials[0]` cut to 40 runes (37 runes and `...` when longer). Do not change `source.DenialsText` (the TUI uses it), `EngineRun.Denials`, or `--json`.
6. Part (c), docs: `docs/dashboard.md:660-668` (a sentence: `ork status` prints the count and the first denial cut to 40 characters; `ork status --json` lists every denial; the Overview rows are as before), `docs/state.md:486-493`, and `docs/design.md:1697-1701`.
7. CHANGELOG, last, so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict: add one entry at the bottom of `## Unreleased` that starts "Claude fallback implementer:" and says: the Claude implementer's brief lists its allowed shell commands and the rules for them (*proposed*); `ork status` shows a count of denied commands and the first one cut short (*proposed*).
8. Mutation-check each new assertion (remove the vendor condition, the role condition, the 40-character cut, the rune cut) and report which test went red.
9. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

Owner decisions (2026-11-08): What is left of part (a) after S277? (Open question Q1 in the slice's Why section; no adj record decides it, so the implementer cannot start part (a)) -> a2 extra doneWhen items: add Claude-only rules to `doneWhen` after the S277 "Allowed forms" item in `internal/engine/brief.go`, using the existing `Allow` field and no new section. The rules are: change files with Edit and Write; no `sed -i`, scripts, heredocs, redirects, `&&` or `;`. The brief tests then check `## Done when` items.. How should the orchestrator-only Check line `rg -n "Bash" internal/roles/prompts/` be handled? -> replace: drop the line and rely on `TestNoClaudeCodeOnlyMechanics` (`internal/roles/roles_test.go`), which forbids the word Bash in a prompt. It already runs in the `go -C WORKTREE test ... ./internal/roles` line. Keep `git -C WORKTREE diff --stat -- internal/roles` as the "prompts untouched" check. Done when both exit 0 with no diff output..

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./internal/engine ./internal/cli ./internal/roles ./internal/tui` (the TUI goldens must not change: `git -C WORKTREE status --short testdata/golden` prints nothing).
- `rg -n "Bash" internal/roles/prompts/` prints nothing (the prompts stay vendor-neutral), and `git -C WORKTREE diff --stat -- internal/roles` is empty.
- [HUMAN CHECK] `ork status` in a terminal at 100x30 and 80x24 with a run that has five long denied commands: the denied part is one bounded piece of the run's line (about 70 characters), not several lines of command text.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] After the daemon is restarted on the landed build, the next Claude stand-in implementer run (Codex out of credits) is watched once: its brief holds the `## Shell commands` section, and status shows the short denied count.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Claude fallback implementer: shell rules in the brief, short denied count".
